case.title: The Missing Traveler
case.description: Matej vanished from Zhelejov, leaving behind his horse and several paid nights. The record of his departure looks far too convenient.
direction.paper: Question {{rumorSource.directionLabel}} in {{settlement.displayName}} or search for the records yourself.
direction.witness: Find {{witness.directionLabel}} and ask about Matej's horse.
direction.overheard: Listen to the conversations around the inn.
direction.ledger: Lavrentiy hid the guest ledger in one of the upstairs chests. Someone else wrote Matej's departure line, so the book is worth examining.
dialogue.rumor.henryMissing: I hear one of your guests disappeared.
dialogue.rumor.innkeeperLeft: He did not disappear. He left before dawn. At least, that is what the guest ledger says.
dialogue.rumor.henryHorse: Then why leave his horse behind?
dialogue.rumor.innkeeperHorse: That is what troubles me. He paid three nights ahead, then vanished. By morning his horse was back in the stable, already unsaddled.
dialogue.rumor.henryName: What was his name? What brought him here?
dialogue.rumor.innkeeperMatej: Matej. A petty merchant. He was carrying money to a companion's widow — the man died on the road, and Matej swore his family would receive their share.
dialogue.rumor.innkeeperHand: Not me. The line appeared that morning, in a hand I did not know. I locked the book away after that.
dialogue.rumor.innkeeperChest: It is upstairs. I hid it in one of the chests. I will not give you a key. If someone wrote a lie in my book, I would rather not know how you reached it.
dialogue.rumor.foundHenryHand: You did not write the line saying Matej left.
dialogue.rumor.foundInnkeeperChest: So you got to the ledger after all. You could not have had a key.
dialogue.rumor.foundHenryNote: The hand is different. And the note between the pages says someone lured him past the old willow.
dialogue.rumor.foundInnkeeperHorse: Then he did not leave of his own accord. His horse came back without him and was in the stable before dawn.
dialogue.rumor.foundInnkeeperBoguslav: I do not know. Bretislav was with the horses that night. If he saw anything, he will not speak of it willingly.
dialogue.witness.henryHorse: You tend the horses. Do you remember the merchant Matej's mount?
dialogue.witness.bretislavRemembers: A bay, white fetlock on the hind leg. Matej rode out in the night. Before dawn, the horse was back in its stall.
dialogue.witness.bretislavReturned: A local man led it in. Mud on his boots, something dark on his sleeve. He said Matej had continued on foot.
dialogue.witness.bretislavSaw: Clearly enough. He pressed a coin into my hand and told me to forget who held the reins.
dialogue.witness.bretislavWarning: The next day a dead crow lay on my threshold. I understood. Not every truth is worth one's neck.
dialogue.witness.bretislavFire: Later he burned something by the old willow. It smelled of scorched wool. In the morning I found a blackened clasp from a travelling cloak.
dialogue.witness.henryPoint: You will point this man out to me.
dialogue.witness.bretislavPoint: I will. But after that, you and I never spoke.
objective.witness.name: Question the farmhand Bretislav
objective.witness.active: Lavrentiy said Matej's horse returned without its rider. The farmhand Bretislav may have seen who brought it back.
objective.witness.done: Bretislav saw a local man return Matej's horse alone, then burn something by the road. He identified the suspect.
objective.witness.fallbackDone: Bretislav saw a local man return Matej's horse alone and destroy evidence by the road. He identified the suspect.
dialogue.overheard.matejArgument: I heard Matej arguing with someone behind the inn. He kept saying the money was not his, that a widow was waiting for it.
dialogue.overheard.widowMoney: I heard it too. The other man said silver would not bring her dead husband back.
dialogue.overheard.goneByDawn: Matej was gone before dawn. Seems the argument settled itself.
document.ledger.name: Torn Guest-Ledger Page
document.ledger.info: A page from the Zhelejov inn ledger. The departure line is in another hand, and a note was hidden between the leaves.
document.ledger.body:
Matej of Ledetchko. Three nights paid.

Left before matins.

The last line is written in darker ink and another hand. A folded scrap lies between the pages:

If I do not return, the money in my purse belongs to Marketa, Pavel's widow. A local man learned of it and spent the evening asking how much I carried and who expected me. At dawn he means to show me a shorter road past the old willow.

He is too obliging for a man who wants nothing from me. But if I am wrong, I shall be far away by noon.

Matej
journal.rumor: Matej's horse returned without its rider, and the record of his departure is doubtful.
journal.ledger: The departure entry was forged. Someone knew about Matej's money.
journal.witness: {{witness.displayLabel}} saw the man who returned Matej's horse.
journal.overheard: The argument before Matej vanished concerned the widow's money.
trophy.description: A red feather taken from {{target.displayLabel}}. A silent reminder that Matej's debt was finally collected.
